jobs.title: Academic Coach at College Living Experience
jobs.description: Employer: College Living Experience Expires: 11/19/2026 Young Adult Transition ProgramJob Type: Part-timeHours: Approximately 15 hours per weekWork Location: In person – Austin, TXStart Date: ASAPPay: $18-$20 per hour Are you looking for a job where your work truly matters, every day is different, and you get to be part of a fun and supportive community? At College Living Experience (CLE), academic success isn't built through grades alone. It happens during study sessions, conversations with professors, time-management planning, problem-solving challenges, and the everyday moments where students learn how to navigate college with greater confidence and independence. As an Academic Coach, you'll help neurodiverse young adults discover how they learn best and develop the skills needed to succeed in college and beyond. You'll work alongside students to strengthen executive functioning, organization, study habits, self-advocacy, and academic confidence while helping them navigate the challenges of higher education. We are looking for someone who is patient, creative, and passionate about helping students reach their potential. Someone who enjoys mentoring, adapting their approach to different learning styles, and celebrating growth along the way. Candidates often come from backgrounds in education, tutoring, special education, academic coaching, psychology, student support services, learning assistance, or humanities instruction. We especially welcome candidates with experience teaching or tutoring writing, English, literature, history, communications, philosophy, political science, or related fields. In this role, you'll provide individualized academic coaching and tutoring, help students develop effective study strategies, manage assignments and deadlines, communicate with professors, prepare for exams, and build the skills needed to become more independent learners. You'll collaborate closely with our social, career, and independent living teams to ensure students receive holistic support across all areas of their development.The ideal candidate believes that success looks different for every student and is excited to help neurodiverse young adults build confidence, overcome challenges, achieve their educational goals, and create a strong foundation for lifelong learning and independence. Why People Love Working at CLE Working at CLE means being part of a collaborative team dedicated to helping students achieve meaningful academic and personal growth. Every day is different. You'll work one-on-one with students, helping them navigate college coursework, develop effective learning strategies, and overcome challenges that may be impacting their success. You get to see real progress. One of the most rewarding aspects of this role is watching students gain confidence, improve their academic skills, and become more independent learners. You can be creative in your approach. No two students learn the same way. You'll have the flexibility to adapt strategies, develop individualized supports, and find innovative ways to help students succeed. You build meaningful relationships. Academic coaching at CLE goes beyond tutoring. You'll serve as a mentor, guide, and advocate as students navigate their college experience. You're part of a supportive team. Our academic, career, social, and independent living staff work closely together to provide holistic support and celebrate student successes. Academic Coaching & Executive Functioning Support Provide individualized academic coaching and tutoring based on each student's learning style, strengths, and academic goals. Review syllabi, assignments, grades, and course requirements to help students create realistic semester and weekly plans. Teach and reinforce executive functioning skills, including organization, time management, prioritization, task initiation, and study strategies. Help students prepare for exams, complete projects, and develop effective note-taking and learning techniques. Support students in communicating with professors, academic advisors, and campus Disability Support Services (DSS) when appropriate. Foster self-advocacy, problem-solving, and independent learning skills. Student Support & Collaboration Build strong mentoring relationships that encourage accountability, confidence, and personal growth. Collaborate with social, career development, and independent living staff to ensure students receive coordinated support across all domains. Participate in team meetings, student reviews, and problem-solving discussions. Documentation & Communication Document student progress, coaching sessions, and action plans in BestNotes following each student meeting. Communicate concerns, successes, and recommendations to the Academic Coordinator and interdisciplinary team. Maintain accurate records and support student goal tracking throughout the semester. BenefitsCLE offers a supportive work environment and benefits for eligible employees, which may include:• Dental insurance• Vision insurance• Retirement plan• Paid sick time• Flexible scheduling optionsRequirements Transportation RequirementsThis role includes travel between work sites and transporting students as needed.Applicants must:• Possess a valid driver’s license• Have at least one year of licensed driving experience• Meet company motor vehicle insurance requirements Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in psychology, education, social work, counseling, or a related field Teaching/tutoring experience (1+ year preferred). Experience supporting students with learning differences or special education (preferred). Strong communication skills and the ability to tailor instruction to individual learning needs. Strong organizational and problem-solving abilities Ability to work both independently and collaboratively within a team environment

jobs.title: Afterschool Group Leader at Immigrant Social Services
jobs.description: Employer: Immigrant Social Services Expires: 11/19/2026 2026–2027 Afterschool Programs Group LeaderPosition SummaryImmigrant Social Services, Inc. (ISS) is seeking enthusiastic, dependable, and compassionate individuals who are passionate about making a positive difference in the lives of children and families. Group Leaders play an important role in creating safe, engaging, and inclusive afterschool environments where students can learn, build confidence, develop meaningful relationships, and discover their strengths.Serving students in Pre-K through Grade 5, Group Leaders facilitate homework support, enrichment activities, recreation, and evidence-based social-emotional learning experiences that promote academic success and healthy youth development. Every interaction—from helping a student solve a challenging homework problem to leading a cooperative game or supporting a child through a difficult moment—is an opportunity to foster resilience, confidence, and lifelong skills.Group Leaders receive comprehensive training and ongoing coaching to facilitate evidence-based curricula that strengthen students' social-emotional competencies, build protective factors, and promote healthy decision-making. Group Leaders are more than activity leaders—they are mentors, educators, and trusted adults who help children develop the skills they need to thrive both in and beyond the classroom.About ISS Afterschool ProgramsServing students in Pre-K through Grade 5, Immigrant Social Services (ISS) operates afterschool programs at public school sites throughout Manhattan’s Lower East Side and Chinatown. We see the out-of-school time space as an opportunity to reimagine learning, achievement, and youth development in ways that respond to the lived realities, strengths, and aspirations of immigrant students and their families.Social-emotional learning (SEL) forms the core of our afterschool programs. Through evidence-based SEL experiences, students develop the skills and mindsets they need to navigate relationships, manage emotions, solve problems, make responsible decisions, and build confidence and resilience. Whether helping a student work through a challenging homework problem, facilitating a cooperative game, or supporting a child through a difficult moment, every interaction is an opportunity to strengthen social-emotional skills and promote healthy development.Our work is grounded in Positive Youth Development (PYD), which recognizes young people as capable, resourceful individuals with strengths, ideas, and contributions to make. We create environments where students can build meaningful relationships with adults and peers, develop a sense of belonging, exercise agency, explore their interests, and experience success. Rather than focusing only on what young people need to overcome, our programs intentionally cultivate the protective factors, relationships, and opportunities that help children thrive.Within this SEL and Positive Youth Development framework, group leaders facilitate homework support, enrichment, recreation, and hands-on learning experiences that promote academic success and whole-child development. Program activities and curricular content integrate language arts and literacy, STEM, social studies, the arts, health and fitness, and social and emotional development—while creating space for curiosity, creativity, critical thinking, collaboration, and compassion.Core ResponsibilitiesCreate Safe, Inclusive, and Supportive Learning EnvironmentsGroup Leaders help create spaces where every child feels physically and emotionally safe, welcomed, and valued.Responsibilities include:Supervise students and ensure their safety and wellbeing throughout all afterschool activities.Foster a welcoming, culturally responsive, and trauma-informed environment where children feel respected, included, and encouraged to participate.Build caring, supportive relationships that promote trust, belonging, and positive youth development.Encourage cooperation, responsibility, and respect through positive behavior support,and developmentally appropriate classroom management.Model professionalism, empathy, patience, and positive communication in all interactions with students, families, school staff, and colleagues.Recognize and respond appropriately to students' individual developmental, social emotional, and behavioral needs.Support Students Throughout the Afterschool ExperienceEvery afternoon is different. Group Leaders help create a smooth, engaging, and supportive afterschool experience by confidently guiding groups of students through a variety of activities, settings, and learning experiences. Success in this role requires flexibility, sound judgment, and the ability to adapt to students' changing needs throughout the day.Group Leaders are responsible for:Guiding students through the many parts of the afterschool day, including arrival, snack, homework, enrichment, recreation, and dismissal.Supervising students in a variety of settings, including classrooms, cafeterias, gymnasiums, playgrounds, hallways, and other shared spaces.Leading safe, organized, and positive transitions between activities while maintaining student engagement and appropriate behavior.Providing academic support and facilitating homework support in both small- and large-group settings.Recognizing when students need additional encouragement, redirection, or emotional support and responding with patience, empathy, and professionalism.Creating opportunities throughout the afternoon for students to practice leadership, cooperation, communication, and responsible decision-making.Facilitate Social-Emotional Learning ISS believes children develop important life skills through meaningful relationships, engaging learning experiences, and opportunities to practice positive behaviors every day. Group Leaders play an active role in helping students build the knowledge, skills, and confidence needed to succeed in school and life.After completing ISS training and receiving ongoing coaching, Group Leaders facilitate evidence-based Social-Emotional Learning (SEL) curricula while reinforcing these skills throughout daily interactions, activities, and routines.Group Leaders help students develop:Self-awareness and self-confidenceSelf-management and emotional regulationResponsible decision-makingPositive relationship skillsSocial awareness and empathyCommunication and conflict resolution skillsProblem-solving and critical thinkingLeadership, teamwork, and cooperationBy integrating these skills into homework support, enrichment activities, recreation, and everyday interactions, Group Leaders help children build habits that contribute to long-term academic success and healthy development.Collaboration & Professional ResponsibilitiesHigh-quality afterschool programs are built through teamwork, communication, and a shared commitment to helping children succeed. Group Leaders work closely with Site Directors, fellow staff, school personnel, and families to provide a consistent, supportive experience for every student.Responsibilities include:Collaborate with Site Directors, school staff, and fellow Group Leaders to provide engaging, high-quality programming.Communicate professionally with colleagues, families, and school personnel to support student success and well-being.Promptly report concerns related to student safety, attendance, behavior, or well-being to supervisory staff.Participate actively in staff meetings, trainings, coaching sessions, and professional development opportunities.Maintain accurate attendance, lesson implementation records, and other required program documentation.Carry out responsibilities in accordance with ISS's mission, positive youth development philosophy, and organizational values.QualificationsWe're looking for individuals who enjoy working with children, are eager to learn, and are excited to make a positive impact in their community.Required QualificationsCurrently enrolled in college or have completed some college coursework.At least 18 years of age.Experience working with children in schools, afterschool programs, camps, tutoring programs, childcare settings, or other youth-serving organizations.Experience leading activities or facilitating groups of children.Ability to work during afterschool hours throughout the school year.Strong communication and interpersonal skills.Dependable, professional, and committed to creating a positive experience for children.Preferred QualificationsAbility to build supportive relationships with children and families from diverse cultural and linguistic backgrounds.Effective classroom management and positive behavior support skills.Strong situational judgment and adaptability, with the ability to recognize what each moment calls for—whether supporting an individual student, guiding a small group, managing transitions, or leading engaging activities for a larger group.Comfortable working in an active, fast-paced environment where schedules, settings, and student needs change throughout the afternoon.Willingness to receive coaching and implement evidence-based curricula with fidelity.Commitment to continuous professional growth and reflective practice.Bilingual in Mandarin, Cantonese, Fujianese, or Spanish preferred.Experience working with immigrant, multilingual, and underserved communities is highly desirable.Why Join ISS?At ISS, you'll do more than supervise children after school—you'll become part of a mission-driven organization dedicated to strengthening immigrant communities through education, prevention, and youth development.As an ISS Group Leader, you'll gain valuable professional experience while making a lasting impact on the lives of children and families. Whether you're pursuing a career in education, psychology, counseling, social work, public health, or another care profession, this position provides meaningful opportunities to develop practical skills that will support your future career.What You'll GainHands-on experience working with elementary-aged children in a school-based setting.Paid training in evidence-based Social-Emotional Learning (SEL) curricula.Coaching from experienced youth development professionals.Experience facilitating engaging lessons, enrichment activities, and group discussions.Leadership, communication, and problem-solving skills that transfer across education and human services careers.Experience working with culturally and linguistically diverse children and families.Opportunities to build your resume while making a meaningful difference in your community.At ISS, we believe investing in our staff is essential to providing high-quality programs for children. We are committed to supporting your growth as a youth development professional through training, mentorship, and continuous learning.Hours and Commitment: This is a part-time/contract position for the 2026-27 school year that follows the NYC DOE academic calendar. Must be available during afterschool hours, Monday–Friday, 2:00 pm/2:30 pm – 5:45 pm/6:00 pm (start and end times depend on location). Flexible days, but five days a week is preferred. Hiring is contingent upon passing a background check. Location: Our afterschool programs operate at public school sites in the Lower East Side/Chinatown neighborhood.Payrate: $17.00 - $18.00 per hour - depending on experienceApplication Process:To apply, please email your resume and cover letter to hr@issnyc.org with the subject line: Afterschool Programs Group Leader. About ISSFounded in 1972, Immigrant Social Services, Inc. (ISS) is a non-profit organization dedicated to improving the conditions of underserved immigrants in Chinatown/Lower East Side, New York City. The majority of immigrant families we serve are from low-income, monolingual Chinese-speaking multigenerational households. Through programs and services centered on care, education, prevention, and community, we nurture and empower immigrant children/youth, young adults, seniors, and families to develop and restore their agency to strengthen the wellbeing of their communities. For more information, visit www.issnyc.org. Equal Opportunity EmploymentImmigrant Social Services, Inc. (ISS) is an equal opportunity and affirmative action employer. Qualified applicants will receive consideration without regard to their race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or status as a protected veteran.

jobs.description: Employer: LEAD Charter School Expires: 11/19/2026 THE ROLELEAD Charter School seeks an exceptional Special Education Teacher to join our mission-driven community. Our goal is to transform equity through opportunities for young people in Newark. Our innovative model re-engages students through active participation in rigorous, relevant content and standards-driven, competency-based instruction aligned with market demands. Reporting to the Head of School, teachers at LEAD embody commitment, energy, and passion, facing challenges with the support, feedback, and collaboration of teammates and school leaders.WHO WE AREThe mission of LEAD is to enable students ages 16-21 in grades 9-12 to master essential skills for success in careers, postsecondary education, and community leadership within a global society. jobs.title: High School Special Education Teacher at Environmental Charter School
jobs.description: Employer: Environmental Charter School Expires: 11/19/2026 The Environmental Charter School is seeking a highly dedicated and motivated Special Education Teacher for our upcoming school year (2026-27). Successful candidates must be progressive-minded and embody a can-do spirit and work ethic. For best consideration, candidates should have a degree or experience in education, a strong work ethic, and a “whatever it takes” attitude.OUR PHILOSOPHY AND MISSIONAs the world changes and becomes increasingly more complex, global citizens will need to be equipped with skills to be flexible thinkers, creative problem solvers, and effective leaders. ECS offers a program that develops students into critical thinkers, thoughtful innovators, and well-rounded scholars. We provide students with the tools and educational foundation to become tomorrow’s global citizens, and we strive to teach students how their choices impact the world around them. By using environmental content as a lens for instruction, ECS provides students with a context in which to explore ideas and observations, to practice inquiry, and to actively problem-solve. Throughout their academic career at ECS, students build core skills across all disciplines and then actively apply these skills to support the impact of learning.WORKING AT THE ENVIRONMENTAL CHARTER SCHOOLThe Environmental Charter School’s faculty and staff are passionate, talented, and uncompromising with a mission to make sure all students succeed at a high level. Every aspect of our organization and program is designed and continually refined to ensure that goal. Our work is student-centered, constantly improving, and reflective. ECS’s progressive approach to education challenges faculty to take risks. We strongly value collaboration and recognize the power of systems thinking. Our high achievement scores, long waiting list (nearly 200 students in kindergarten alone!), and unique location in the city of Pittsburgh serve as a model in environmentally focused education.OVERVIEWThe ECS Special Education Teacher is an intervention, differentiation, and curriculum adaptation specialist. Working collaboratively with general education teachers, education assistants, paraprofessionals, building specialists, and the Campus Leadership Team, the ECS special education teacher provides the modifications and adaptations that students need to participate in rigorous and engaging learning opportunities in the classroom. Special education teachers work to ensure all students (K-5) are supported through case management across or within grade levels as determined by the Campus Leadership Team. Candidates should be energetic and progressive-minded, with a willingness to work collaboratively with the building staff.KEY RESPONSIBILITIESWorks with the general education teachers to modify and adapt curriculum and PBL experiences for students with disabilities based upon a variety of instructional techniquesCollaborates with parents, administrators, school psychologists, and other professionals to develop individualized education programs (IEPs) designed to promote students’ educational, physical, and social/emotional development Provides instruction or instructional supports in all academic subjects using a variety of techniques to reinforce learning and to meet students’ varying needs and interestsProvides direct and indirect instructional support to students in a variety of settings, including small group, one-on-one, and inclusive classroom settingsFacilitate a positive, achievement-oriented, and structured learning environment in which all students can experience success Implement school-wide behavior management policies and the Olweus Bullying Prevention program within classrooms and throughout the schoolMaintain accurate and complete student records and prepare reports required by laws, district policies, and administrative regulations in a timely and professional manner Collect and maintain data to track student progress, drive individualized instruction, and to design academic interventionsMaintain professional competence by participating in opportunities for professional growthServe as the case manager for students with IEPs and communicate regularly with families to share academic and behavioral progress and develop a supportive home-school relationship Educational Background and Work ExperienceBachelor’s degree from an accredited institution PA Certification in special education; dual certification in Math or ELA preferredAt least 3 years of teaching experience preferredFamiliarity with charter schools and high school students desirableCompensation and BenefitsMinimum starting salary of $44,716 plus a $1000 special education supplement. Additional compensation may be awarded to highly qualified individuals.Comprehensive benefits package including medical, dental, vision, life, short-term, and long-term disability insurance, generous paid time off, and participation in a generous 403b retirement plan, and voluntary coverage optionsTo ApplyPlease submit a cover letter, resume, and a copy of your current PA certification to: https://ecspgh.org/careers/.Clearances current within one year of hire date will be required and include Arrest & Conviction Disclosure, Pennsylvania Child Abuse History Clearance (Act 151), Pennsylvania State Police Criminal Record Clearance (Act 34), and FBI Criminal Background Check (Act 114). Commonwealth of PA Sexual Misconduct/Abuse Disclosure. Release (Act 168) will also be required.ECS is an equal opportunity employer.

jobs.description: Employer: University of Texas Permian Basin Expires: 11/19/2026 Assistant Professor of Biology (Tenure-track) Hiring Department The University of Texas Permian Basin welcomes applications for our Assistant Professor of Biology. Applicants must have a Ph.D. in a biological field and research interests in the areas of evolutionary or organismal biology, ecology, or related fields. The selected candidate must develop a research program that involves undergraduate and graduate students and must be able to teach advanced undergraduate courses in animal behavior, evolution, ecology, and vertebrate zoology, as well as graduate courses in the area of research interest. The ability to teach large introductory-level biology courses is a plus. The anticipated start date is August 2026. Review will occur on a rolling basis until the position is filled. Salary Range $65,000.00 depending on qualifications Essential Functions Tenure track faculty at UTPB teach 18 credit hours per year (60%), with expectations for research (30%) and service (10%) to the department, university, and discipline. The successful candidate will teach undergraduate and graduate courses to support instructional needs. A willingness to develop and teach online graduate courses is desired. The successful candidate is expected to maintain a research program involving undergraduate and/or graduate students. A willingness to apply for extramural support for his/her research is desired. Position duties include: • Teach courses based on need and expertise • Conduct research related to one's expertise and apply for extramural support as deemed appropriate • Engage undergraduate and graduate students in research • Provide academic advising to undergraduate and graduate students • Actively participate in the department's recruitment and expansion • Participate in curricular development • Provide additional services to the university, college, and department as needed Required Qualifications 1. Ph.D. in Biology or a closely related field Preferred Qualifications 1. Commitment to working with a diverse student population2. Willingness to seek extramural funding for research3. Teaching experience at the college level (can include laboratories taught as a graduateteaching assistant) Additional Information From the Department UT Permian Basin is located in West Texas (halfway between El Paso and Dallas). The Midland/Odessa area is accessible through the Midland International Air and Space Port (MAF) and has several Texas State Parks and U.S. National Parks located within 200 miles of the university. The Department of Biology currently has 6 full-time faculty (2 associate professors, and 4 lecturers), a robust undergraduate program (>200 majors), a successful prehealth professions program (>70% acceptance to medical school), and a growing graduate program (~ 10 students). Please contact Dr. Athenia Oldham mailto:(oldham_a@utpb.edu) if you have questions. Required Application Materials 1. Cover Letter2. Curriculum Vitae (CV)3. List of References4. Teaching Philosophy Statement (limit to one page)5. Research Statement (limit to one page)6. Transcripts (Preferred)7. Letters of Recommendation (Preferred) Conditions of Employment 1. The job description is not a complete list of all responsibilities and duties performed by employees. Employees may perform other related duties as assigned by their immediate supervisor.2. Employment is subject to an introductory period to monitor employee performance.3. Once hired, the prospective employee must present documentation within three (3) days of the hire date to establish their identity and employment eligibility as required by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). Applicants must be able to show proof of eligibility to work in the United States by time of hire. UTPB participates in e-Verify.4. Employees must be able and willing to travel and perform duties away from campus as necessary and must be able to operate a licensed motor vehicle, have access to a dependable motor vehicle, and possess a valid state driver's license. Must have and maintain a satisfactory driver's record.5. Employment is contingent upon a successful background check.6. UT Permian Basin is an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or status as a protected veteran. Schedule Generally, the normal work hours for the university are Monday through Thursday, 7:30 - 5:30 pm; Friday, 8:00 am - 12:00 pm with a one-hour lunch. The individual holding this position may need to be available early morning, evening, and on weekends to meet the needs of the department. Faculty hours may differ based on class schedule and department need. Standard Working Conditions 1. Able to lift various materials up to 25 pounds on an occasional basis.2. Able to bend, crouch, and reach continuously.3. Physically able remain seated, frequently to continuously.4. Able to remain standing up to 15% of the time.5. Possesses dexterity abilities required to perform job duties including extensive keyboard work, operating office equipment, performing filing, and other job-related responsibilities that include extensive wrist and hand movement.6. Standard working conditions may differ depending on department and occupation. University Benefits 1. UT Permian Basin offers an excellent compensation package including heath, retirement, & fringe benefits for eligible employees.2. Coverage includes medical, prescriptions, life insurance, AD&D, and matching retirement provided by UTPB.3. You may also be eligible to add dental, vision, family coverage, & flex-spending accounts, additional retirement, and a few other coverages as options too.4. Fringe benefits include tuition reimbursement (after one year of service), wellness breaks, employee assistant program (EAP), and meal deals, among other perks and discounts!5. Our benefits package, along with an ample leave policy, make for a great total compensation package. About the University The University of Texas Permian Basin is located in Odessa, Texas. It was authorized by the Texas Legislature in 1969 and founded in 1973. The Permian Basin is one of the fastest-growing, culturally vibrant, economically invigorated regions of the country - full of industry, culture, and wide-open spaces. At the academic heart of this area sits The University of Texas Permian Basin - which every year, delivers smart, savvy leaders across the U.S. As a regional, comprehensive institution, The University of Texas Permian Basin serves a diverse community of students from the region, the state, and beyond. Through excellence in student-centered teaching, learning, research, and public service, the University cultivates engaged citizens and impacts lives while advancing the technology and public interests of West Texas. Our vision is that the University of Texas Permian Basin will be an innovative, responsive university that thinks large and lives local. We will lead in advancing education, research, economic competitiveness, and cultural enrichment.Visit our social media sites below for more information. jobs.description: Employer: Cuesta College Expires: 11/19/2026 Toddler & Preschool Assistant Teacher (Children's Center)Cuesta CollegeSalary: $44,928.00 - $54,612.00 AnnuallyJob Type: Full Time - 11 Months/ 100% FTEJob Number: FY2627-00075Location: North County Campus, CADepartment: InstructionClosing: 11/18/2026 11:59 PM PacificJob Description SummaryDEFINITIONUnder the general supervision of the Instructional Assistant (Lead Classroom Teacher), and Children's Center Director, support, all activities related to the children's classroom environment at the Cuesta College Early Childhood Education program. This includes supervising and guiding toddler or preschool children in developmentally appropriate social, emotional, physical, language, creative and cognitive activities. Assistant teachers should be able to communicate effectively with children, staff, students, faculty and parents.DISTINGUISHING CHARACTERISTICSThe Assistant Teacher must have the ability to demonstrate appropriate guidance practices and procedures taught through the Cuesta College Early Childhood Education program. Applicant must be able to model respectful, responsive, and reciprocal interaction as part of the daily curriculum.This position supports and promotes student learning outcomes and institutional effectiveness by ensuring a quality program and services for children and their families and ensuring compliance with State licensing requirements.ABOUT THE COLLEGEWhere You Will WorkServing all of San Luis Obispo County, Cuesta College has provided comprehensive associate degree offerings, certificates, and community programs to the region since 1964. The main campus is located along scenic Highway 1, west of San Luis Obispo and east of the beaches of the Pacific Ocean. Cuesta College has a North County Campus in Paso Robles, and South County Center, in Arroyo Grande.Who We AreEquity, diversity, and inclusion are essential to our culture and the work we do. Cuesta College is proud to be a designated Hispanic-Serving Institution (HSI) committed to racial and socio-economic diversity as it reflects our communities and student populations. We actively seek to attract candidates who share this commitment to equity, diversity, and inclusion. As part of the Cuesta College team, you can expect to be part of a collaborative community of faculty, classified professionals, administrators, students, and community partners advancing educational excellence with intentional support services leading to student success and completion. - Additional information about the college can be found at https://www.cuesta.edu/about/index.html- The college planning documents can be found at https://www.cuesta.edu/about/collegeplans/index.html- Our Student Equity Action Plan can be found at https://www.cuesta.edu/about/info/student-equity-initiatives/equity/index.html- We offer comprehensive benefit options. Information about benefits can be found at https://www.cuesta.edu/about/human-resources/benefits/index.html Essential Functions & QualificationsESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS - Support the Instructional Assistant/Lead Teacher in all aspects of the classroom environment;- Participate in planning weekly/monthly lessons, snack menus and classroom activities;- Be a role model for students, children, and families;- Ongoing role modeling and demonstration of Developmentally, Individually, and Culturally Appropriate Practices;- Assist in maintaining a safe and healthy environment;- Willing to lead in the absence of the Instructional Assistant/Lead Teacher;- Be a team player with all center staff and activities;- Support cooperative relationships with Instructional Assistant/Lead Teacher, Staff, Parents, Students and Faculty;- Willingness to participate in yearly rotation from toddler room through the preschool classrooms, practicing continuity by rotating with same groups of children;- Participate in assessing and conferencing with families about their children; and- Perform other related duties as required. QUALIFICATIONSEducation:Required - Minimum 24 ECE and general education units equal to an Associate of Arts Degree- 12 units of ECE must include the core courses including child/human growth & development, child/family/community or child family relations; and program/curriculum. Applicant must have a minimum of three semester units or four quarter units in each of the core areas.- Knowledge of philosophies of the Program for Infant and Toddler Care.- To have completed or have the ability to take a 3-unit infant and toddler course (as required by licensing for work with infants and toddlers) within one year of employment.- Must be enrolled and maintain continued enrollment in coursework leading to an AA/AS or BA/BS degree in Child Development, other related field or a BA/BS in any other discipline Experience:Required - Minimum one year experience working in a CA State Licensed preschool or toddler center based program working 3 hours per day as an employee, laboratory student or combination of the two Preferred - Completion of Laboratory or Supervised Field Experience equal to ECE 216;- Experience working in a college ECE laboratory school. Knowledge of: - Current technologies, personal computer, and associated office software such as word processing, spreadsheet, presentation, and/or database software;- Correct usage of English, grammar, spelling, punctuation, and vocabulary; and- District policies and procedures. Ability to: - Establish and maintain cooperative working relationships with those contacted in the performance of duties; and- Demonstrate a sensitivity to and understanding of the diverse academic, socioeconomic, cultural, and ethnic backgrounds of staff and students and of staff and students with physical and learning disabilities. Physical ability to: - Read and comprehend printed matter and text and data on computer monitors;- See for the purpose of reading children's books, laws and codes, rules and policies and other printed matter;- Hear and understand speech at normal levels;- Understand and carry out oral and written directions;- Communicate intelligibly and effectively via speech, telephone, written correspondence, and/or email;- Sit or stand for extended periods of time both indoors and outdoors;- Bend, twist, push and pull, stoop, kneel, crawl, and climb;- Lift and/or carry 50 pounds for the purpose of picking up and lifting a child;- Sit on floor and/or small tables and chairs;- Exert manual dexterity sufficient for keyboard and other office equipment operation; and- Perform other duties as requested. License and Certificates:Required - Hold or willing to apply for a Child Development Permit at the Associate Teacher level or above;- Possess or obtain current First Aid and CPR Certification;- Possess a current California driver's license;- Current TB Clearance;- Up to date with all required immunizations according to the Department of Social Services, Community Care Licensing; must include Measles and Pertussis, Flu preferred. Additional InformationREQUIRED DOCUMENTS TO APPLYCandidates will be required to submit ALL of the required documents below when applying for this position. When uploading documents, PDF uploads are preferred. - Cover letter;- Resume;- Reference List (see further instructions below);- Unofficial transcripts;- Diversity statement (see further instructions below). Diversity Statement Instructions: Cuesta College is committed to building and maintaining a workforce that reflects and honors the diversity of our students. jobs.description: Employer: Bishop Baraga Academy Expires: 11/19/2026 Lead Teacher/Montessori Guide Preschool## What if working in childcare felt different?You love working with children. But that doesn’t mean you have to love **chaos, unpredictable schedules, working weekends, or feeling burned out.**At **Bishop Baraga Academy**, we’ve intentionally built a different kind of childcare and preschool workplace.🌿 **Montessori changes your day.** Our thoughtfully prepared classrooms encourage children to become increasingly independent—which means less entertaining and managing and more **guiding, observing, teaching, and building relationships.**### You might be a great fit for BBA if you are:- **Punctual and dependable** — people can count on you.- **Energetic and positive** — you genuinely enjoy engaging with young children.- **Excited to teach** — you enjoy modeling behaviors and introducing new ideas.- **Kind and patient** — you use a calm, respectful teaching voice, even during difficult moments.- **A positive role model** — you know children are always learning from the adults around them.- **Ready to grow** — you welcome coaching, feedback, professional development, and courses.- **Focused on independence** — you enjoy teaching children to do things for themselves.**Montessori experience? Great! No Montessori experience? We can teach you.**### And here's what you can expect from us:🎓 **You are an educator—not a babysitter.** You will be treated like a professional teacher and Montessori Guide doing meaningful work that goes far beyond supervising play.🤝 **A team you will want to work with.** Supportive teammates, strong leadership, and a tight-knit community of families.📋 **A professionally operated workplace.** We aren't family-run. BBA operates with established policies, procedures, leadership, expectations, and employee benefits.🛡️ **Licensing rules matter.** You will never be expected to knowingly break licensing rules to make staffing or scheduling easier.🏡 **A life outside of work matters, too.** **No weekends. 10 paid holidays PLUS 10 additional paid days off.** Predictable scheduling and real time away from work.❤️ **Work with a purpose.** Spend your days helping children become capable, confident, kind, and independent within a Catholic Montessori community where your work matters.**If you want to be treated like an educator, do meaningful work, be part of a professional team, and still have a life outside of your job—we invite you to join us.**

jobs.title: Strength and Conditioning Coach at Peak Performance Training - Maryville
jobs.description: Employer: Peak Performance Training - Maryville Expires: 11/19/2026 AboutPeak Performance Training Peak Performance Training is a coaching-first strength and conditioning facility in Maryville, TN, serving youth athletes and adults. Our tagline is Climb Higher - we believe capability can be built, consistency beats intensity, and coaching begins with understanding the person in front of you before prescribing anything. We're not chasing hype or quick fixes. We're building real relationships and real, evidence-based development, one session at a time. The RoleThis is a coaching-first position. Your job is to deliver high-quality, high-energy sessions that meet Peak's coaching standard, and to run a coaching process that drives real client development - for athletes and adults both. Peak believes coaches, not programs, are what actually change people's trajectories. This role exists because we believe that, and we're looking for someone who believes it too. We're not looking for someone who already knows our system - we'll teach you that. We're looking for someone who wants to give back through coaching, who's a student of the craft, and who we can trust to represent Peak on the floor. What You'll DoDeliver Peak's coaching standard every session: Explain–Cue–Demo, visual language, 1:1 feedback, full engagement with every athlete and client in the room Come prepared - know what, who, and how you're coaching each week, before the week starts Log PRs and milestones for your athletes and clients Keep equipment and facility standards tight Work through a structured onboarding: culture and coaching fundamentals first, then technical systems, then live reps with feedback, extending into adult coaching once trust is established Participate in a real review rhythm - weekly check-ins, weekly programming meetings, and quarterly performance reviews - not a "figure it out yourself" environment. Talent Leadership & Organizational Effectiveness - Cultivate an engaged and high-performing team through effective hiring, onboarding, coaching, performance management, communication, and professional development while fostering an inclusive, collaborative, and accountable workplace culture.- Cultivate a team climate that engages staff and trainers to live NWTC's values and accomplish CTED and team goals and objectives.- Establish clear instructional and performance expectations for trainers and provide ongoing coaching, feedback, observation, and professional development to strengthen teaching effectiveness and learner outcomes.- Conduct performance reviews and training observations to evaluate instructional effectiveness, provide meaningful feedback, establish performance expectations, and support continuous improvement in teaching practice and learner outcomes.- Collaborate with Talent & Culture and CTED leadership to attract, select, onboard, and retain qualified trainers who demonstrate industry expertise and a commitment to effective teaching and learner success.- Provide leadership for resolving employee, customer, learner, trainer, and business partner concerns using effective communication, problem-solving, and customer service practices, escalating complex or significant concerns to the Dean as appropriate. Operational & Resource Management - Make recommendations regarding budgeting, resource allocation, facilities, equipment, purchasing, and scheduling to maximize operational efficiency and effectively support contract training fulfillment.- Manage and implement approved resource allocation, facilities, equipment, purchasing, and scheduling priorities to support effective delivery of customized contract training and workforce development programs.- Monitor departmental expenditures and resource utilization to ensure alignment with approved budgets, operational priorities, and College requirements.- Utilize operational and financial data to evaluate effectiveness, identify trends and opportunities, and inform planning and resource decisions.- Determine workload for shared faculty among academic programs and provide recommendations regarding course scheduling to meet training needs across the district. Learner Success & Learning Environment - Promote learner success by ensuring customized training programs provide safe, inclusive, engaging, and effective learning environments across delivery locations and modalities.- Provide leadership in addressing learner concerns, challenging classroom behavior, complaints, and other barriers to learning in collaboration with trainers, CTED leadership, and appropriate College partners.- Partner with Academic Affairs & Workforce Development, Student Affairs, and other internal stakeholders to align customized training with College policies, learner-support practices, instructional quality expectations, and pathways to additional College learning opportunities.- Use learner, instructional, customer, and program outcome data to identify opportunities to strengthen learner engagement, completion, satisfaction, instructional quality, and workforce outcomes. College, Community & Continuous Improvement - In coordination with the College's Community Impact Coordinators, leaders, and other staff, represent CTED and the College with business, industry, K-12, community, advisory, and workforce partners to understand regional needs, strengthen relationships, and advance College and regional workforce priorities.- Participate in College committees and cross-functional initiatives to inform policies, programs, resource decisions, and strategies affecting customized training, learner success, and workforce development.- Implement and monitor policies and procedures that support compliance with College, State, Federal, District, Wisconsin Statute 38.14 Contracts for Services, safety, and applicable program requirements.- Collaborate with CTED leadership, Academic Affairs & Workforce Development, and other College partners to enhance the College's approach to workforce partnerships, evaluate program effectiveness, apply data-informed improvement strategies, and continuously strengthen training quality, operational practices, and workforce impact. jobs.title: Event Staff - Charleston, SC at Event Partners Inc. (EPI)
jobs.description: Employer: Event Partners Inc. (EPI) Expires: 11/19/2026 Be part of the action. Work the events you love. At EPI, you don't just work a job—you get to be part of the experience. Our event staff are on the front lines of professional and collegiate sporting events, concerts, festivals, and major events throughout the Charleston area. If you enjoy being around people, thrive in a fast-paced environment, and want a job where no two events are exactly the same, EPI gives you the opportunity to experience live events from a completely different perspective. From the moment the gates open to the final whistle, encore, or closing announcement, you are part of making the event happen. What You'll Do: EPI provides event management and staffing for a wide variety of live events. Depending on the event, you may work in roles including: Parking and traffic operationsTicket taking and guest entrySecurity screeningUshers and guest servicesCrowd managementHospitality and suite servicesAccess controlBarricade operationsBack-of-house event operationsAnd much moreYou could spend one shift helping fans find their seats at a college football game, the next assisting with a concert, and another working behind the scenes at a major festival. Every event is different. Every shift is an opportunity to be part of something happening in your community. This is a PART-TIME, EVENT-BASED opportunity serving the Charleston, South Carolina area. Our schedules are built around live events, which means this is a great opportunity for individuals looking for flexible part-time work while still wanting to be involved in an exciting environment. Whether you're looking for additional income, enjoy sports and entertainment, want to meet new people, or simply want a job that's more interesting than sitting behind a desk, EPI puts you where the action is. You'll gain valuable experience in customer service, event operations, communication, teamwork, and problem-solving—all while working alongside a team responsible for helping some of the area's biggest events run successfully. Who We're Looking For We are looking for people who are: Reliable – If you accept a shift, we need you to show up and be ready to work.Outgoing – You're comfortable interacting with guests and working with a team.Energetic – Live events move quickly, and we need people who can keep up.Professional – You represent EPI and our clients every time you put on the uniform.Team-oriented – Great events happen when everyone works together.Customer-focused – You can remain friendly and professional, even when situations get challenging. RequirementsMust be 18 years of age or olderMust have a High School Diploma or GEDMust be able to pass a background checkMust maintain a neat and presentable appearanceMust be able to stand and remain active for extended periods of timeMust be able to provide excellent customer service in a variety of situationsMust be dependable and committed to working the shifts you accept Why EPI?Because work doesn't have to feel like work. At EPI, you can experience live sporting events, concerts, festivals, and other major events while playing an important role in making them successful. You're not sitting in the stands—you're behind the scenes, on the field level, at the gates, in the crowd, and in the middle of the action. If you're dependable, energetic, and ready to be part of something bigger than a typical part-time job, we want you on the EPI team.We are an equal opportunity employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, disability, gender identity, marital or veteran status, or any other protected class.

jobs.description: Employer: Psypawlogy Pet Care LLC Expires: 11/19/2026 Psypawlogy Pet Care LLC · Serving clients throughout the DMV area (Washington, DC, Northern Virginia and Maryland)About PsypawlogyPsypawlogy is a psychology-informed pet care company founded by a doctor of psychology, currently serving clients all around the DMV area. We believe pets thrive when care is built around how they think, feel and learn, so we apply principles from behavioral science and psychology to every visit.That means we use positive reinforcement and low-stress handling, and we read each animal's body language to understand how they're feeling. We keep routines consistent so pets feel safe while their people are away, and we offer enrichment that engages their minds as well as their bodies. We also recognize that pet parents trust us with family members, and we strengthen the human-animal bond through clear communication and thoughtful updates.Every visit follows The Psypawlogy Method, our standard of care for safe, calm and enriching pet care. Specialists who join us gain hands-on experience applying these principles. That makes this a great fit for anyone studying psychology, animal behavior, veterinary science or a related field.About this opportunityThis is an independent contractor opportunity, not employment. You run your own schedule, choose the services you offer, and accept or decline each job as it comes. There are no minimum hours, and you're free to work with other clients and platforms. It's a great fit for students and anyone who wants flexible, meaningful work with animals.Services you can choose to offerDog walkingDrop-in visitsCat and small-animal careOvernight and extended-stay pet sittingHouse sittingDaycareAdventure Club outingsPuppy care and socializationPet transportation through the Psypawlogy Pack Bus (optional, with your own vehicle and auto insurance)Wedding concierge, birthday parties, doggy socials, community walks and vendor eventsCompensationYou earn 65% of the client fee for each service you complete, including add-ons and holiday rates.Tips are passed through to you in full.You receive a share of cancellation fees on jobs you accepted.You're paid weekly by direct deposit.Each job shows its pay before you accept it.As an independent contractor, you're responsible for your own taxes and receive a Form 1099-NEC.RequirementsAt least 18 years oldCurrent Pet CPR and First Aid certificationCompletion of a background check, with your written authorizationA smartphone and reliable transportation to client homes across the DMV areaComfort with dogs and cats of all sizes, and the judgment to follow client care instructions and safety proceduresFor transportation, a valid driver's license and auto insurance that covers business useWhat we provideAccess to our client network and scheduling platform, Psypawlogy branded identification, a welcoming community of animal lovers, and liability coverage during Psypawlogy jobs, subject to policy terms.To applySubmit your resume and a letter of interest through Handshake. jobs.title: Special Education Behavior Intervention Teacher at STRIDE Academy
jobs.description: Employer: STRIDE Academy Expires: 11/19/2026 STRIDE Academy in St. Cloud, MN, stands out as a K-8 public charter school with a strong focus on the whole child, celebrated for fostering academic excellence and a nurturing learning environment. Our mission emphasizes individualized learning and innovative teaching, preparing students for future success. Notable for our community involvement and award-winning programs, STRIDE offers a unique, supportive educational experience that cultivates curiosity and character development, making a significant impact on our students and the wider community. POSITION DETAILSTitle: Special Education Behavior Intervention TeacherGrade: 8Start Date: 2026-2027Full Time FTE: 1.0 POSITION OVERVIEWThe Eighth Grade Special Education Teacher provides individualized academic instruction and targeted behavior intervention for eighth-grade students with disabilities at STRIDE Academy. This position combines the instructional and case management responsibilities of a special education teacher with a focus on helping students strengthen self-regulation, engagement, and the skills needed to access learning and make academic progress.The teacher develops and implements Individualized Education Programs (IEPs), delivers specially designed instruction, and uses academic and behavioral data to guide student supports. Working with general education teachers, paraprofessionals, related service providers, administration, and families, the teacher creates a safe, structured, and inclusive learning environment and supports students as they prepare for high school. ESSENTIAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIESAcademic Instruction and Student ProgressPlan and deliver specially designed instruction in reading, writing, mathematics, and other identified areas based on student needs and IEP goals.Develop lesson plans, instructional materials, and assessments that support access to eighth-grade curriculum and address individual skill gaps.Provide individual, small-group, and classroom-based instruction as determined by student IEPs and service needs.Implement accommodations, modifications, assistive technology, and other supports to increase student participation and independence.Collect and analyze assessment results, work samples, and progress monitoring data; adjust instruction and interventions to improve student outcomes.Teach organization, task initiation, work completion, study skills, self-advocacy, and other executive functioning skills that support academic success.Behavior Assessment and InterventionConduct functional behavioral assessments (FBAs) as part of the evaluation and IEP team process; collect and analyze data to identify behavior patterns, contributing factors, and student support needs.Develop, implement, monitor, and revise Positive Behavior Support Plans (PBSPs) or Behavior Intervention Plans (BIPs) with the IEP team and align supports with student IEPs.Provide explicit instruction in self-regulation, coping strategies, social skills, problem-solving, and replacement behaviors that support participation in learning.Establish predictable routines, clear expectations, positive reinforcement, and individualized supports that promote safety, responsibility, and engagement.Use approved prevention and de-escalation strategies, respond to behavioral crises within training and school procedures, and support students in returning to instruction.Document behavioral incidents and intervention outcomes; collaborate with administration and the special education team regarding disciplinary removals, readmission supports, and required procedures or reporting.Use restrictive procedures only when authorized, trained, and permitted by applicable law and school procedures; complete required documentation and participate in follow-up reviews.IEP Case Management and ComplianceServe as the special education case manager for assigned students and coordinate IEP development, implementation, annual reviews, and progress reporting.Coordinate and participate in evaluations and reevaluations; facilitate IEP and Evaluation Summary Report (ESR) meetings and complete required special education documentation.Maintain accurate, timely records of services, academic and behavioral progress, parent communication, assessments, and due process documentation.Coordinate service schedules and communicate student accommodations, modifications, and behavior supports to staff responsible for implementation.Work with the IEP team to ensure services and documentation meet applicable federal and Minnesota special education requirements and school procedures.Collaborate with families, receiving high school staff, and the IEP team to support the transition to ninth grade, including sharing relevant instructional and behavior supports and completing transition planning as applicable.Collaboration and Student SupportPartner with eighth-grade teachers to align instruction, coordinate assignments and assessments, and support student access to general education settings.Guide assigned paraprofessionals in implementing instructional plans, accommodations, and behavior supports; provide modeling, feedback, and clear daily expectations.Communicate regularly and professionally with parents and guardians about student strengths, needs, progress, and strategies for support.Collaborate with related service providers, school leadership, and Child Study or CARE Teams as assigned to address academic, behavioral, social-emotional, and attendance concerns.Build positive student relationships and support routines across classrooms, hallways, lunch, arrival, dismissal, and transportation settings as relevant to assigned students.Reinforce schoolwide expectations and use restorative problem-solving approaches consistent with student plans and school practices.Professional ResponsibilitiesParticipate in professional development, professional learning communities, staff meetings, and assigned student support teams.Maintain required crisis prevention and intervention training, such as CPI or Ukeru, as applicable to the assignment; provide staff training only when qualified and authorized.Protect student confidentiality, maintain professional boundaries, and meet schedules, deadlines, and professional responsibilities.Perform other related duties as assigned.REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONSBachelor’s degree required; Preferably in Special Education, Social Work, Psychology or related fieldValid Minnesota teaching license in special education appropriate to the assigned grade level and students served, or eligibility to obtain the required license before beginning the assignment.Three or more years of experience working with students with behavioral and social-emotional needs in school settings.Knowledge of specially designed instruction, differentiated teaching, assessment, IEP development, due process requirements, and progress monitoring.Demonstrated knowledge of FBAs, individualized behavior plans, positive behavior supports, and crisis prevention and de-escalation strategies.Ability to deliver academic instruction while supporting students with significant behavioral and social-emotional needs.Preferred QualificationsExperience teaching middle school students, managing a special education caseload, and supporting students with emotional or behavioral disabilities.Training in trauma-informed practices, restorative approaches, and approved crisis prevention and intervention methods.Skills & CompetenciesStrong instructional planning, classroom management, organization, and documentation skills.Ability to analyze academic and behavioral data and adjust instruction and supports accordingly.Clear, respectful communication and effective collaboration with students, staff, and families.Ability to remain calm, consistent, and supportive during challenging situations.Proficiency with educational technology and student data systems.Commitment to individualized learning, equitable practices, and the academic and personal growth of every student. BENEFITS AND COMPENSATION Salary Range: Starting salary of $60,000 or higher based on experience per contract yearBenefits: Comprehensive benefits package including health insurance, retirement, and professional development opportunities APPLICATION PROCESSApplication Materials: Submit a resume, cover letter, references, and complete online application Application Deadline: Until FilledContact Information: Niki Krier, Special Education Director, nkrier@strideacademy.orgApply here: https://www.strideacademy.org/employment EQUAL OPPORTUNITY STATEMENT STRIDE Academy is committed to creating a diverse environment and is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status. CALL TO ACTION Join our dedicated team at STRIDE Academy and make a difference in the lives of our students. Apply today to contribute to our vibrant learning community where every child is encouraged to reach their full potential. We look forward to welcoming you to our team!

jobs.title: Special Education Support Specialist at Rochester Beacon Academy
jobs.description: Employer: Rochester Beacon Academy Expires: 11/19/2026 SPECIAL EDUCATION SUPPORT SPECIALISTRochester Beacon Academy is seeking a Special Education Support Specialist for the 2026-2027 school year. Rochester Beacon Academy (RBA) is a 6th-12th grade charter school that places a strong emphasis on providing individualized attention to students. The school has small class sizes, allowing teachers to provide students with focused and personalized instruction. RBA also has a special focus on serving students with special education needs, with close to 80% of the student body receiving such services. The administration and staff are dedicated to providing these students with the support and resources they need to succeed in school and beyond. RBA has a caring and compassionate culture, with teachers and staff committed to creating a safe, joyful and inclusive learning environment. The administration places a high value on work-life balance for both students and staff, recognizing the importance of a healthy work-life balance for academic success. In addition, the school uses trauma-informed practices to support and respect students in ways that acknowledge and address the impact of past traumatic experiences. These practices help create a safe and supportive learning environment that promotes emotional healing and academic success. Overall, the charter school is a small, caring educational institution that is committed to providing a supportive and inclusive learning environment for students, particularly those with special education needs.Your job responsibilities includes but are not limited to:Schedule IEPs and evaluation meetings.Upload IEPs and related information into SPED forms.Organize daily transportation routes, communication, etc.Maintain staff calling trees and voicemails through Marco.Transfer SPED records to all appropriate agencies (Bluestem, Prairie Care, etc).Assign subs for licensed and non-licensed staff daily due to PTO schedule.Maintain all SPED paper files in a concise and accurate manner that meets compliance with the State of MN.Support program staff.Be available to answer to stakeholders on inclement weather days (WILD Days).Knowledgeable of all office equipment.Knowledgeable about all district policy.Assists with organizing of records, maintaining of Special Education student folders, and other permanent records assigned and while protecting confidentiality of student records and information. Schedules students for testing and assessment appointments. Provides support in Special Education enrollment and identification.Participate in department and program training and meetings.Facilitates successful monitoring and completion of compliance checklists of IEPs as meetings occur.This job description is not intended to be all-inclusive, and employees will also perform other reasonable related business duties as assigned by their immediate supervisor and other management.Minimum Qualifications: High School Diploma or equivalent Clerical/Office experience Knowledge of Microsoft Office Programs Knowledge of SPED FormsKnowledge of Special Education timelines in compliance with MDE.Ability to organize tasks and complete within desired deadline Attention to detailPay: $36,000.00 - $55,000.00 per year based on experience and qualificationsBenefits:Dental insuranceHealth insuranceHealth savings accountLife insurancePaid time offRetirement planVision insuranceSchedule and Location:Full TimeMonday to Friday In PersonRochester, MN 55902: Relocate before starting work (Required)If interested in applying, please complete the following:1. Current resume2. Cover Letter3. Copy of Teaching License if present4. 2 Letters of Recommendation or ReferencesCompleted materials can be emailed to our Executive Director at beth.bruns@rochesterbeaconacademy.org

jobs.title: High School Exceptional Education Teacher at LEAD Public Schools
jobs.description: Employer: LEAD Public Schools Expires: 11/19/2026 JOB TITLE: Special Education Teacher (Exceptional Education)REPORTS TO: Principal Be a LEADer: Teach Exceptional Education at LEAD Public SchoolsSpecial Education (Ex.Ed) teachers are champions for equality within the school, ensuring that students’ needs are met. Our ideal Special Education teacher is passionate about supporting students with IEPs, advocating for those who need the most support, and continually growing as an educator. Flexibility, coachability, and a commitment to excellence are key qualities for this role. The LEAD EnvironmentEx.Ed teachers at LEAD work relentlessly with their teammates to:Enhance students’ reading abilities, enabling them to explore historical events and gain a broader understanding of the world.Help students meet Tennessee standards by the end of the year.This work is supported through:Coaching and support from administration.Regular feedback and collaboration with colleagues.Data analysis and targeted instruction to help students overcome challenges and rise above grade-level expectations. What We Are Looking ForSuccessful teachers at LEAD:Put in extra effort to ensure students have access to a high-quality education.Persevere through challenges, set ambitious goals, and never give up on students.Are flexible, hard-working, and committed to improving their classroom abilities to meet students’ needs.We are seeking Exceptional Education teachers who embody these qualities. Position ResponsibilitiesPrimary ResponsibilitiesDesign and implement data-driven lesson plans to support students with cognitive and/or developmental delays.Develop individualized education programs (IEPs) for students.Maintain special education files (both paper and electronic) in compliance with federal, state, and local guidelines.Collect data on individual student skills to measure progress toward IEP goals and assess program effectiveness.Provide functional curriculum and focus on daily living skills, as appropriate.Foster independence in students across all natural settings.Advocate for and facilitate students’ exposure to general education peers and settings, as appropriate.Plan and implement instructional and/or behavioral strategies to ensure all students can access academic content.Other ResponsibilitiesDirect and supervise education assistants to provide effective classroom programs and address individual student needs.Support general classroom teachers in implementing established curricula and individual student plans. QualificationsExperience:Minimum of two years teaching experience preferred but not required.Prior experience with diverse student populations or in an urban setting preferred.Education/Certification:Bachelor’s degree required.Must hold:(a) A valid Tennessee teaching license with the appropriate endorsement to teach SPED, OR(b) A valid out-of-state license transferable to Tennessee within 90 days of employment, OR(c) Proof of progress toward Tennessee certification.Physical Demands:Light to medium physical work involving standing, walking, lifting, pushing, and carrying (exerting up to 20 pounds).Other Qualifications or Characteristics:Belief in LEAD’s mission that all students are capable of success while preparing them for college and life.Evidence of self-motivation and willingness to be a team player.COMPENSATION AND BENEFITSLEAD Public Schools offers an innovative performance-based compensation plan for teachers. This plan allows us to transparently reward our teachers not by how many years they have worked but rather by their positive impact on students and schools, evidenced by their consistent performance in and out of the classroom. Teachers receive a competitive base salary with the potential for a signing bonus and can earn up to 10% on their base salary each year through our performance-based compensation plan. This plan has been in place for 5 years, and we have seen an average annual increase of over 5% for our teachers with approximately 80% retention for those who qualify. Additionally, teachers are eligible for LEAD’s Master Teacher program after 3 years. In this program, teachers can earn up to $100,000 and receive a $1,500 professional development stipend. Robust and competitive benefits package including medical, dental, vision, disability, supplemental insurance, life insurance policy options, and mental health benefits. Application for these benefits may be made immediately upon employment. The policy is effective upon the first of the month following the first day of work.Certificated staff have access to the Tennessee Consolidated Retirement System pension plan (TCRS). Eligible staff contribute 5%, and LEAD matches up to 6%. Staff may also be eligible for 401k, in which LEAD will contribute 5%. Participation in TCRS is mandated by the state of TN. Non-TCRS eligible staff members are eligible to participate in LEAD’s defined contribution 403b plan. LEAD matches 50% of the first 6% of employee contributions. Additional annual contributions are provided to eligible employees after one year based on LEAD’s overall budget performance. Participation in this plan is voluntary.The time off package for school-year employees (teachers, counselors, paraprofessionals) includes 30 paid days during the school year (including holidays, fall break, thanksgiving break, winter break, and spring break). School-year employees also receive summer break. In addition to breaks and holidays, school-year employees can accrue up to 10 PTO days during the school year. The time off package for calendar-year employees (Central office, Instructional Managers, Assistant Principals) includes 32 paid days during the school year (including holidays, fall break, thanksgiving break, winter break, spring break). In addition to breaks and holidays, school-year employees can accrue up to 12 PTO days during the school year. Parental leave - 16 weeks of paid maternity leave and 6 weeks of paid parental leave (adoption, foster care). Teachers are provided with laptop computers with access to the internet and or email to assist them in performing their job responsibilities. APPLICATION PROCESSTo apply, please complete the online application at LEAD Public Schools. LEAD Public Schools Non-Discrimination PolicyLEAD Public Schools does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, creed, religion, ancestry, sex, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, medical condition, national origin, age, pregnancy, physical or mental disability, genetic information, or veteran status in admission to, access to, or operation of its programs and activities. LEAD Public Schools does not discriminate in its hiring or employment practices and complies with applicable federal and state regulations, including those implementing Title IX of the Education Amendment of 1972, Title VI, Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 and Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) 1990.
